scenario.name: CISA ICS-ALERT-10-196-01, Symantec Dossier & MITRE ICS — SIMATIC STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll Interception & S7comm PLC Logic Audit
scenario.overview: Picture a fenced municipal power substation and waterworks yard lined with tall ceramic insulator towers, heavy steel water pipes, red manual valve wheels, and a glass control room. Breaching the fenced perimeter of the municipal power substation, an impostor connects a handheld controller straight into the yard’s switchboard cabinet. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the high-voltage breaker & pipe valve, then smuggles copied records out past the substation fenced entry gate in tiny disguised batches. The grid shift engineer notices the physical breaker clank outside disagrees with the frozen green gauge on the desk and pulls the mechanical override. In this scenario (T1574.001, CISA ICS-ALERT-10-196-01, Symantec Dossier & MITRE ICS, SIMATIC STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll Interception & S7comm PLC Logic Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: engineering Workstation STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll, then s7comm Port 102 PLC Block Download, then s7comm Upload Block Readback Spoofing. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Engineering Workstation STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll, then S7comm Port 102 PLC Block Download, then S7comm Upload Block Readback Spoofing, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 7 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1574.001 - Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Search Order Hijacking)
stages.description: Breaching the fenced perimeter of the municipal power substation, an impostor connects a handheld controller straight into the yard’s switchboard cabinet. stages.title: Stage 2: S7comm Port 102 PLC Block Download (OB1, OB35 & System Data Block SDB)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter)
stages.description: Sending unauthorized commands along the control wire, the impostor trips the main high-voltage breaker arm and cranks the heavy waterworks valve wheel off balance. Here in Step 2 inside the power substation, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the high-voltage breaker & pipe valve without disturbing the isolated backup generator bay. stages.title: Stage 3: S7comm Upload Block (0x1D) Readback Spoofing & Offline Checksum Verification
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1564 - Hide Artifacts)
stages.description: Even as lights flicker across the district and pressure climbs inside the pipes, a falsified dial inside the glass control room keeps displaying steady green readings. In this final step inside the power substation, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the substation fenced entry gate in tiny disguised batches until the control room gauge recorder catches the mismatch. On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ s7comm port=102 func=0x1D (Upload Block) OB1 wire_bytes=2940 gui_displayed_bytes=412 / ⇠#3 RESP 29) from Node ③ (#3 s7otbxdx.dll API Wrapper) to Node ④ (#4 PLC CPU 315-2 / 417 (:102)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Profibus Frequency Converter Bus).
